Every method runs or is accounted for in the fixed order ARP, DNS, DHCP, AD, LLDP/CDP, SNMPv3, API; completed or failed stages need non-overlapping timestamps, AD/SNMPv3/API completion needs a credential reference (never a value, and SNMP community fields are rejected), and any stage without a result needs an explicit reason. Findings must be private addresses inside the declared scope; devices are merged across methods by MAC or IP with a confidence from the number of independent methods, and LLDP/CDP neighbours become explicit links. scripts/Export-LocalDiscovery.ps1 produces a real run from a Windows host's own ARP cache, DNS client cache and DHCP/gateway configuration without sending packets.

restrictions: ARP, DNS and DHCP stages were exercised on a real Windows host from its own caches; LLDP/CDP, SNMPv3, controller APIs and AD enumeration have no authorized lab yet and are accepted as validated source-report contracts with explicit not-available reasons. No active scan is performed and the real run data (private addresses) is not stored in this repository.

CG-009.reason: Scale to 20,000 devices is delivered as a distributed design plus a measured single-node result. The collector-capacity registry models site collectors reporting to regional relays and one central node (never one PC for every device), excludes offline collectors from usable capacity, compares it with the 20,000-device target and makes over-capacity collectors, uncovered sites, single points of failure, missing upstreams and a missing central node explicit. scripts/scale-benchmark.js ingested 20000 devices on this Windows PC at 5696 devices/s with every measured view under the 500 ms budget (assets first page 7.5ms, assets last page 199.4ms, assets search by hostname 9ms, dashboard 109ms, summary 0.3ms, evidence readiness 84.3ms, discovery sequences registry 9.7ms).

CG-010.reason: Optional, opt-in agents for managed devices are delivered as two read-only collectors and a validated report contract. scripts/agent/CyberGuard-Agent.ps1 reports Windows Security/System/Application event-log health, Sysmon presence, services, process names (no command lines) and AV/EDR/firewall state with signature age; scripts/agent/cyberguard-agent.sh reports auditd, journald and syslog health, systemd services, process names and ClamAV/Falco/EDR/firewall service state. CG-012.reason: Malware, ransomware, protection-disabling and suspicious-process detection is delivered as six versioned rules in lib/detection-rules.js evaluated on every stored evidence record of their kind: known malicious command patterns (shadow-copy/backup deletion, disabled recovery, encoded PowerShell, certutil download, remote mshta/rundll32/regsvr32), unsigned processes creating services or tasks, unsigned user-path processes contacting public addresses, unauthorized deliberate disabling of AV/EDR/firewall/logging/agents, ransomware indicators and managed devices without active AV/EDR. CG-017.reason: Just-in-time privileges are implemented inside CyberGuard itself, not as source evidence. A viewer or analyst requests a higher role with a scope, a written reason (10+ characters), a duration of 5-480 minutes and an action cap of 1-500; only one open request per user; approval or denial must come from a different user whose standing (non-temporary) role is administrator. On approval the session role is raised immediately and drops back automatically at expiry or when the action cap is consumed (every elevated state-changing request counts); grants can be revoked at any time. Every request, approval, denial, revocation and elevated action is written to the append-only audit log. Settings is now reachable by every role so non-admins can request.

CG-020.reason: The firewall rule analyser (lib/firewall-analyzer.js) checks the latest ruleset per device: duplicates; redundant and shadowed rules for first-match vendors; allow rules overridden by a covering block for Windows deny-overrides; any-any allows; inbound administrative ports (explicit admin ports, or any TCP/UDP port without an application, service or keyword scope) open to any address; broad inbound rules; stale rules from hit data; expired or soon-expiring exceptions; and change impact against the previous ruleset of the same device, including new administrative exposure. Coverage understands CIDR containment, port ranges, protocols, direction, profiles and scope constraints (owner, package, service, local/remote user, interface, ICMP type, port keywords). CG-024.reason: Vulnerability assessment runs only inside a declared, approved scope: vulnerability.assessment_scope records the assessment id, authorization reference, approver, time window (at most 366 days), target assets and/or networks (IPv4/IPv6 CIDR) and permitted methods, limited to installed-version matching and passive exposure evidence (active scanning is rejected). Only software inventories observed inside the window for in-scope assets are assessed; out-of-scope devices and inventories outside the window are listed and not assessed. Findings are enriched from the public sources named in the requirement through scripts/vuln-feed-to-telemetry.js and lib/vulnerability-intel.js: CISA KEV JSON (date added, due date, known ransomware use), FIRST EPSS CSV or API (probability and percentile) and NVD CVE API 2.0 (CVSS score, version, vector, attack vector, user interaction, CWE); NVD application CPE matches become version-range catalogs keeping every release-track range (inclusive, exclusive and exact bounds, Windows display-name aliases). The converter splits output into files under the 2 MiB ingest limit. Exposure attributes per asset come from data already collected (observed open services, remote-service events, inbound allow-from-any firewall rules, public addresses); a finding counts as remotely reachable only when its CVSS vector is network, needs no user interaction and the asset accepts inbound connections, while flaws that need a user to open content are reported separately. Feed freshness is reported (KEV and EPSS stale after 7 days, NVD after 30). A KEV-listed vulnerable finding in an active assessment raises CG-VULN-KEV-024 (critical when remotely reachable). Catalog parsing and name matching are indexed and cached per catalog version (about 45 ms per assessment on a 20,820-range catalog). The overview card shows the assessment summary.

Exposure is evidence of reachability, not proof of exploitability; nothing is scanned or exploited. Ordering by KEV, EPSS and CVSS is not the risk ranking of CG-025.

CG-025.reason: Vulnerability risk is ranked per finding of active, authorized assessments by a transparent additive score (0-100) rather than CVSS alone: exploitation evidence (CISA KEV 35; otherwise EPSS bands 28/20/10/3), exposure (network vector without user interaction on a reachable asset 25 internet / 18 network; needs user interaction 8; adjacent 10; local or physical 3; unknown 10), asset importance from asset.context (service criticality 15/11/6/2 plus restricted 5 or confidential 3 data; default 8 when no context) and CVSS severity (CVSS x 1.5, default 7). Existing controls subtract only when recorded with evidence: enforced network segmentation and blocked internet access (only for reachable findings), enforced entry MFA, operational monitoring (asset.compensating_controls) and an active EDR or antivirus with signatures at most 7 days old (agent.inventory_report), at most 20 points. Each finding lists every factor with its points and evidence in English and Arabic, marks missing inputs, flags KEV findings past the CISA due date, and shows its CVSS-only rank next to its risk rank; bands are critical >= 75, high >= 55, medium >= 35. Critical findings raise CG-VULN-RISK-025. The model is returned with every response and shown in the interface.
tests: tests/domain.test.js: vulnerability risk ranks by exploitation evidence, exposure, asset importance and evidenced controls, not CVSS alone
tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads

Live run on a real Windows workstation with the CISA KEV, NVD and FIRST EPSS feeds, its firewall rules and its agent report: 143 findings ranked, 141 placed differently from a CVSS-only order
restrictions: The weights are a documented engineering model, not a calibrated industry standard; they prioritise remediation work and do not prove exploitability. Asset importance and compensating controls come only from recorded asset.context and asset.compensating_controls evidence; when absent the score uses a marked default weight.

CG-026.reason: Three validation tiers are defined in lib/validation-tiers.js and enforced on every validation.test_plan. Passive: only evidence-review techniques (telemetry review, log analysis, inventory correlation, config export review), nothing reaches the targets. Low-impact authorized validation: only allow-listed read-only or single-request checks (version banner, credentialed config, credentialed patch, TLS configuration, safe port reachability, registry policy) and, when approved, an authorization reference, an approver, a window of at most 14 days, a rate limit of at most 60 per minute and at least one stop condition. Adversary emulation: only MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs, only in a lab environment, and when approved two different approvers, isolation evidence and a rollback plan, within at most 30 days. Plans breaking a rule are rejected with a specific reason. Every validation.test_run is compared with its approved plan: unknown or unapproved plans, runs outside the window, techniques not in the plan and targets outside the plan (asset references or CIDR) are flagged out-of-plan, excluded from the plan results and alerted as CG-VALIDATION-OUT-OF-PLAN-026. scripts/Invoke-LowImpactValidation.ps1 performs a real low-impact validation of the local Windows host (SMBv1, RDP NLA, LLMNR, UAC, firewall profiles, antivirus signature age) using only registry reads and local cmdlets and writes a validation.test_run; CI runs it on the Windows runner. CyberGuard governs and records tests; it does not execute attacks.
tests: tests/domain.test.js: validation tiers enforce passive, low-impact and lab-only adversary emulation rules and flag runs outside their approved plan
tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads
tests/ui-contract.test.js: vulnerabilities view shows the three validation tiers, their enforced rules and out-of-plan runs

Real run on a Windows workstation over the HTTP ingest API: approved low-impact plan, 6 read-only checks (4 pass, 2 fail: LLMNR enabled, antivirus signatures 14 days old), and a real run under an unknown plan flagged and alerted
restrictions: Adversary emulation is governed (plans, approvals, lab-only targets, run comparison) but no emulation is executed by CyberGuard and no lab was available, so only the plan side of that tier was exercised. The low-impact script covers local Windows checks; remote low-impact checks against other hosts are not implemented.

CG-027.reason: Detection coverage is measured for every executed technique in an in-plan validation run. lib/domain.js correlates target alerts whose evidence was observed from one minute before the run through fifteen minutes after it, filters validation/vulnerability/inventory alerts out of detection evidence, and waits for the settling window before declaring a gap. An expected alert with target telemetry but no matching alert becomes a rule gap; no target telemetry becomes a visibility gap. The API and bilingual UI show the detection rate, expected detections, matching rule IDs, telemetry count, settling state and both gap types while keeping the validation outcome separate from exploitability. GitHub Actions run 43566724661 executed T1110.001 password guessing on an ephemeral Windows runner, exported and ingested the real Windows Security events, and completed the CG-027 measurement step successfully.
tests: tests/domain.test.js: detection coverage measures alerts during validation runs and records rule and visibility gaps instead of assuming exploitability
tests/http.test.js: detection coverage API exposes measured executions, detection rate and gaps
tests/ui-contract.test.js: vulnerability view shows detection rate, rule gaps, visibility gaps and settling for CG-027
Browser QA: isolated Chromium fixture showed one detected T1110.001 execution, one rule gap and one visibility gap with a 33.3% detection rate
GitHub Actions Windows lab run 43566724661: the disposable-runner password-guessing and detection-measurement step completed successfully at commit 59c692f
restrictions: The GitHub-hosted runner is an ephemeral authorized lab, not a production environment. Anonymous GitHub access confirms that the measurement step completed but does not expose its console result; the system treats either a matching detection or a recorded detection gap as a valid measurement outcome. Coverage depends on validation plans, run evidence, target identity and telemetry timestamps; it does not prove a vulnerability is exploitable or that every attack technique is detectable.

CG-028.reason: Critical production assets are identified from their latest asset.context evidence and protected by a platform safety floor that administrators cannot bypass. Approved production plans permit only passive or low-impact validation; low-impact plans must name each protected asset explicitly, cannot use a network range that contains one, are limited to six checks per minute and five critical assets, and production adversary-emulation plans remain prohibited. Authorized lab emulation is unaffected. The API and bilingual UI expose the enforced floor, protected assets and matching approved plans.
tests: tests/domain.test.js: critical production assets enforce a non-bypassable validation safety floor even for administrators
tests/http.test.js: critical production protection API exposes the enforced floor and protected assets

Browser QA: isolated Chromium fixture showed QA-CRITICAL-028, the approved low-impact plan, administrator bypass prohibited, a 6/minute ceiling and broad network targets prohibited
restrictions: Protection depends on current asset.context.service_criticality evidence; an unclassified asset cannot be inferred to be critical. The policy governs validation plans recorded or ingested through CyberGuard; independent tools outside the platform still require their own network and endpoint enforcement.
